text.title: PR Mentoring Session Protocol Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every PR Mentoring Session Protocol application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: The record MUST carry an `inputs[]` entry `learning_goal` stating exactly one skill in observable terms: what the junior's code or PR will do differently ("writes a migration that is safe to re-run", "asserts on the error type, not on `Exception`"). One goal per session; a second goal is a second record. Goals phrased as attitudes ("be more careful", "think about edge cases") are rejected.

rationale.source: Anders Ericsson and Robert Pool, 'Peak: Secrets from the New Science of Expertise' (2016), on deliberate practice

rule.rationale: Skill improves through focused practice on one specific, measurable sub-skill with immediate feedback; a session that tries to fix five things fixes none, and a goal nobody can observe in the next PR cannot be checked at the next session.

rule.statement: The record MUST carry an `inputs[]` entry `observed_gap` that describes what the code did and what it should have done, and `evidence[]` MUST contain the URL of the specific diff line or review comment where the gap is visible (a GitHub `#discussion_r...` or `#L...` anchor, or the equivalent in GitLab or Bitbucket). A gap with no line-level URL, or one phrased about the person ("sloppy", "rushed") rather than the code, is rejected.

rationale.source: Google Engineering Practices, 'How to do a code review' (eng-practices); Kluger and DeNisi, 'The Effects of Feedback Interventions on Performance', Psychological Bulletin (1996)

rule.rationale: Feedback aimed at the task improves performance; feedback aimed at the self tends to reduce it. A line the junior can open, read and fix is task feedback. "You need to be more thorough" is a judgement with nothing to act on, and a record built from such lines cannot show progress six months later.

rule.statement: Every review comment posted during the session MUST carry a Conventional Comments label (`issue`, `suggestion`, `question`, `nitpick`, `praise`, `thought`) as its first word, and the record MUST carry `inputs[]` counts per label. At least one `praise` comment MUST point at a specific line the junior got right. A session in which `nitpick` comments outnumber all other labels combined is recorded as `learning_goal_not_addressed` and the nits are moved to a formatter or linter task.

rationale.source: Conventional Comments specification (conventionalcomments.org); Google Engineering Practices, 'How to do a code review'

rule.rationale: Unlabelled comments make a blocking design problem and a spacing preference look identical, so the junior fixes the forty easy ones and misses the one that mattered. The label counts are also the only cheap measure of whether the reviewer is teaching or formatting; a formatter does the latter for free.

rule.statement: The senior MUST NOT push commits to the junior's branch during the session. Before any fix is written, the junior restates the gap in their own words and the restatement is recorded in `inputs[]` as `restated_gap`; the fix commit MUST be authored by the junior. A record whose fix commit author is the senior, or that lacks `restated_gap`, fails this rule.

rationale.source: Anders Ericsson and Robert Pool, 'Peak' (2016); widely established practice in engineering mentoring

rule.rationale: A fix the senior types is a fix the junior watched. The restatement is the only point in the session where the reviewer learns whether the junior understood the gap or just agreed to it, and the junior's own commit is what makes the next PR's behaviour attributable to them.

rule.statement: One session covers one PR, and the comments raised in the session are tied to the `learning_goal`. Unrelated problems found in the same PR MUST be recorded in `inputs[]` as `deferred_findings` (line URL plus one line each) and posted as ordinary review comments after the session, not mixed into it. A session record spanning multiple PRs is rejected.

rationale.source: Google Engineering Practices, 'How to do a code review' and 'Small CLs'; Anders Ericsson and Robert Pool, 'Peak' (2016)

rule.rationale: A review that surfaces everything at once teaches nothing in particular. Keeping the session on the one goal, and parking the rest, is what lets the junior connect the specific gap to the specific fix; the deferred list guarantees the other findings are not lost.

rule.statement: `decision` MUST name one follow-up action the junior will demonstrate in a specific next PR or ticket (URL in `evidence[]` once it exists) within a stated window of at most 14 days or the junior's next two PRs, whichever comes first. "Keep this in mind" and "be careful next time" are not follow-up actions. The record is not closed until the follow-up PR URL is added.

rationale.source: Anders Ericsson and Robert Pool, 'Peak' (2016), on feedback loops in deliberate practice; widely established practice in engineering mentoring

rule.rationale: The learning happens in the attempt after the feedback, not in the feedback. Without a named next PR there is nothing to check at the following session, and the same gap gets re-taught from scratch each time because nobody recorded that it was already taught.

rule.statement: If a prior session record exists for the same junior, `evidence[]` MUST link it and `inputs[]` MUST carry `prior_action_status` with one of `demonstrated`, `partial`, `not-demonstrated`, judged from the follow-up PR the prior record named. The same `learning_goal` recorded as `not-demonstrated` three sessions in a row MUST change the intervention (pairing session, structured exercise, course) and be escalated to the engineering manager in `decision`; repeating the same review comment a fourth time is forbidden.

rationale.source: Anders Ericsson and Robert Pool, 'Peak' (2016); widely established practice in engineering management

rule.rationale: Mentoring that does not look back is a sequence of unrelated reviews. The prior-status field is what turns twelve records into a growth curve, and the three-strike escalation is what stops a senior from writing the identical comment for a year while the manager hears nothing.

rule.statement: The record MUST be stored where the junior can read it and the junior MUST confirm the `observed_gap` and `decision` text before the record is committed (confirmation captured as a comment, reaction or commit co-authorship recorded in `evidence[]`). A record kept in a private manager folder, or committed without the junior's confirmation, fails this rule. Aggregated use of the record in performance evaluation MUST be stated in the record at creation time.

rationale.source: Kluger and DeNisi, 'The Effects of Feedback Interventions on Performance', Psychological Bulletin (1996); widely established practice in engineering management

rule.rationale: A hidden dossier is not feedback; it is evidence being collected. The junior who reads and confirms the gap owns it, and can dispute a wrong reading before it becomes a pattern in someone's spreadsheet. The evaluation statement removes the surprise at review time that destroys trust in the whole loop.
